meta.about: SourceRefs retrofitted onto a handful of the EXISTING hand-authored reasoning items in vantage_addon/web/practice.js, as a demonstration of traceability.
meta.important: This file does NOT edit practice.js. The stem/correct_choice/claim are mirrored here read-only so the grounding checker can verify each item traces to a named source span. `claim` is the item's own rationale (the practice.js `explain` string), i.e. the factual statement the card teaches.
meta.source_ref: source_ref = {source_id, start, end} into corpus.json (start/end are inclusive sentence indices).

items.stem: The final sentence about wanting no loss at all mainly serves to:
items.correct_choice: show that the demand for a loss-free translation defeats itself
items.claim: Wanting zero loss means wanting the original, which the reader cannot read, so the demand collapses on itself.

items.stem: The phrase languages carve the world at different joints most directly supports the idea that:
items.correct_choice: different languages divide meaning in non-matching ways
items.claim: If languages carve the world differently, their words do not map one-to-one, which is why a loss-free translation is impossible.

items.stem: The pH barely changes because the added H+ is consumed mainly by:
items.correct_choice: acetate ions acting as a base
items.claim: In a buffer, the conjugate base (acetate) neutralizes added strong acid, so the free hydrogen ion concentration barely rises.

items.stem: Adding a catalyst speeds the reaction because it:
items.correct_choice: lowers the activation energy for both directions
items.claim: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for the forward and reverse directions equally, without shifting the equilibrium.

items.stem: Compound X (unchanged Vmax, increased Km) is acting as a(n):
items.claim: Unchanged maximum velocity with an increased Michaelis constant is the signature of a competitive inhibitor, which competes with substrate at the active site.

items.stem: Under anaerobic conditions, a muscle cell keeps glycolysis running mainly by:
items.correct_choice: fermenting pyruvate to lactate to regenerate NAD+
items.claim: Under anaerobic conditions the electron transport chain stalls, so the muscle cell ferments pyruvate into lactate to regenerate NAD+ and keep glycolysis running.

items.stem: Group B's advantage over Group A best illustrates the:
items.claim: Distributing study across sessions rather than massing it improves long-term retention, which is the spacing effect.

items.stem: Group C doing better through repeated self-testing demonstrates the:
items.claim: Actively recalling information strengthens memory more than rereading it, which is the testing or retrieval-practice effect.

items.stem: The initial pH equals the pKa because, at equal concentrations of acid and conjugate base:
items.correct_choice: the log term in the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation is zero
items.claim: pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]); when [A-] = [HA], log(1) = 0, so pH = pKa.
items.checker_note: The claim is written in math notation ([A-], [HA], log(1)=0) that shares few word tokens with the prose source, so coverage lands right at the cutoff (~0.50). This illustrates the FRAGILITY of a lexical checker near its threshold: symbolic claims are only weakly supported by word overlap and a true entailment model would be needed to judge them robustly. (Observed: passes by a hair; rf_cars_q4, a verbose faithful paraphrase, is the clean false-reject.)
